newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK's United Utilities dismisses CEO.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK's United Utilities dismisses CEO.

text.p: Britain's United Utilities Plc shocked the market on Monday by dismissing its chief executive and warning that current trade was slightly below analysts' expectations.
The electricity and water company's shares sank nearly 10 percent after it said chief executive Brian Staples had left the company due to what it called "a loss of confidence in him by the board".
United Utilities' shares fell 67 pence to close at about 702 pence.

"This is the initial shock that the chief executive's been fired, and there's some comment about trading being below market expectations. So there will be some downwards revisions, I expect, in terms of profitability," said one utilities analyst.
The company's statement did not give details about the reasons for Staples' departure, and a spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
Analysts said the management change and trading statement could indicate more lacklustre results from the company's overseas operations after a previous disappointment in Bangkok.
"I suspect we've only seen a third of the story, and I expect more of the story to emerge over the next few days," said Nigel Hawkins, utilities analyst at Yamaichi.
"That is why the market, understandably, is quite nervous, particularly if there are still mishaps overseas to be reporting," he added.
United said earlier this year it would have to take an 83 million pound ($140 million) charge for losses on a Bangkok sewage contract, which Staples called a "serious disappointment".

The company also disappointed the market last month by posting a lower-than-expected pretax profit of 444 million pounds before exceptionals for the year to March 31 versus 389.2 million a year earlier.
United Utilities named Derek Green, currently managing director of its utility division, as its new chief executive.
"He's plain-speaking and straightforward, with expertise in managing civil engineering aspects of the water and sewerage programme," an analyst said.
The company said Green would remain with the firm until 2000 following the conclusion of price reviews in the water and electricity sectors and Britain's transition to a competitive energy market.
United Utilities said its current trading outlook was satisfactory and added that it was confident about its strategy going forward.
But some analysts noted that United's strategy was less clear than that of Britain's other major multisector utility, Scottish Power Plc.

"Scottish Power has been very clear in saying what it aimed to do in terms of strategy. With United, their strategy is less clear. It may well be that the board thought it was time for a change," Hawkins said.
Staples' departure reflected the hands-on management style of chairman Sir Desmond Pitcher, analysts said.
"This is not the first chief executive that the chairman of this company has fired," said one analyst, noting that former CEO Bob Thian left the firm in similar circumstances a few years ago.
United Utilities was formed in 1995 with the acquisition by North West Water of regional electricity company Norweb. ($ = 0.595 British Pounds)
